rationale: Retain after comparison against all 8,259 labels. Both raws are KO/WT ratios of brain-to-plasma AUC ratios; generic KO/WT brain/plasma ratios lack the protected AUC basis, and the exposure-ratio analogue is not interchangeable with AUC.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. `brain-to-plasma KO/WT exposure enhancement ratio` is an exposure ratio-of-ratios; AUC-specific and point brain/plasma KO/WT candidates have different protected measurement bases.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. The raw explicitly combines total/unspecified brain-to-plasma ratio, Kp,uu,brain, and CSF-to-unbound-plasma ratio; shorter two-measurement candidates would discard one component or its unbound basis.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. The raw combines a point brain/plasma ratio with plasma AUC; ordinary brain/plasma AUC ratios and combined AUC/Cmax ratios do not preserve that asymmetric two-measurement structure.

Retain as the scientifically precise representative after full-catalog comparison. Its 11 explicit KO/WT brain-to-plasma ratio-of-ratios assignments exceed `knockout_to_wildtype_brain_to_plasma_ratio` (2); AUC and exposure KO/WT ratios remain separate.

Merge into the existing retained representative `brain_and_csf_to_serum_ratio` (9 assignments). Its raws describe the same paired brain/serum and CSF/serum measurements as `brain-serum and CSF-serum ratios`, with identical matrices, direction, and point-concentration basis.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. The source is a CsA-induced change in the maternal-brain/plasma AUC ratio, not the underlying maternal AUC ratio itself; merging would erase the protected change endpoint.

Merge into retained `auc_and_cmax` (2 assignments). `Cmax, AUC` and `AUC and Cmax` are order-only variants of the same combined point-maximum and exposure measurements; neither adds a matrix, time window, or direction distinction.
Retain after full-catalog comparison. `Cmax; Te` explicitly combines maximum concentration with Te; candidates containing AUC0-inf, Cmax, and Te add an AUC measurement and are not synonyms.
Retain after full-catalog comparison. This is the only matrix-unspecified combined Cmax-and-trough endpoint; plain Cmax, plain trough, and Cmax/AUC candidates each lose one protected measurement.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. The numerator is CSF amount while the denominator is unbound plasma concentration; CSF concentration, exposure, Cmax, or AUC ratio candidates change the measurement basis.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. `Cmax mean for plasma and cerebrospinal fluid` reports paired CSF and plasma maxima rather than their ratio; CSF/plasma Cmax-ratio labels therefore are not synonyms.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. `AUC CSF/Cu,b` has a CSF AUC numerator and point unbound-brain concentration denominator under the catalog's `b` brain notation; plasma, AUC-denominator, and reverse-direction candidates differ scientifically.

Merge into retained `csf_peak_to_plasma_ratio` (14 assignments). Both labels mean peak/Cmax CSF concentration divided by ordinary corresponding plasma concentration; this does not merge with both-Cmax or peak-plasma-denominator ratios.

Merge into the existing retained representative `csf_peak_to_unbound_plasma_ratio`. Both one-assignment labels describe maximum CSF concentration over free/unbound plasma concentration, preserving the peak numerator and unbound point-concentration denominator.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. Its numerator is CSF exposure but its denominator is unbound plasma concentration; CSF-to-unbound-plasma exposure ratios use exposure on both sides and are not equivalent.
Retain after reviewing all 19 raws against the full catalog. `between` and `CSF and plasma` wording does not establish a numerator; merging into CSF-to-plasma or plasma-to-CSF would invent direction.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. The raw specifies CSF matrix, radioactivity analyte, and maximum concentration; generic CSF radioactivity concentration and matrix-unspecified peak radioactivity candidates each lose a protected dimension.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. `ratio of concentrations in cerebrospinal fluid and serum` leaves numerator direction unstated; explicit CSF-to-serum, serum-to-CSF, peak, steady-state, total, and AUC ratios are distinct.

Merge into existing retained `brain_to_plasma_ratio_and_csf_to_plasma_ratio` (2 assignments). The labels differ only in ordering of the same two explicit ratios; combined-numerator brain-and-CSF/plasma labels remain separate.
Retain after full-catalog comparison. The raw combines CSF/free-plasma AUC and Cmax ratio information; AUC-only and Cmax-only unbound-plasma ratios each omit a protected measurement.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. `Flux ratio (AtoB vs BtoA)` explicitly places A-to-B flux in the numerator; the existing B-to-A-over-A-to-B flux and usual efflux-ratio candidates are inverse directions.

Retain after full-catalog comparison. This is fraction-unbound brain divided by fraction-unbound plasma; `fu_plasma_to_fu_brain_ratio` is its inverse, while Kp,uu uses unbound concentrations rather than fractions.
Retain after full-catalog comparison. The raw explicitly marks an in-vivo-Papp correction to the fu-brain/fu-plasma ratio; merging into the uncorrected ratio would erase the stated correction basis.
